body:
This is likely caused by the model normalization issue in `hermes_cli/model_normalize.py`. 

**Probable root cause:** `_normalize_for_deepseek()` only recognizes `deepseek-chat` and `deepseek-reasoner` as canonical models. When you configure `deepseek-v4-flash`, it gets force-normalized to `deepseek-chat`, which the DeepSeek API now maps to `deepseek-v4-pro` — a more expensive model.

So the charge discrepancy you're seeing (expecting flash pricing, getting pro pricing) is because Hermes is silently rewriting your model name before sending it to the API.

**Check:** Look at your `agent.log` for lines like:
```
Normalized model 'deepseek-v4-flash' to 'deepseek-chat' for deepseek
```

**Our workaround:** We patched `_DEEPSEEK_CANONICAL_MODELS` in `model_normalize.py` to add `deepseek-v4-pro` and `deepseek-v4-flash` so they pass through unchanged. See my comment on #26269 for the patch details.

Also related: #26269 (TUI still shows `deepseek-chat` which the API no longer accepts).
